messages:
maria: heads up — noticed some tenants got silently routed to v1 yesterday even though their tokens had v2 in the header. console shows 'v2 traffic' for them but per-route counts are v1-heavy. anyone seen this mismatch?
aj: hmm, logs? can you paste a sample request id?
maria: sure — req id `r-0a9b3f`. snippet from proxy logs: `X-Client-Version: 2` then later we emit route=v1 in routing decision.
devon: that sounds like the handshake falling back after auth checks. we recently changed the header canonicalization in the auth proxy; could be normalized to `x-client-version` vs `X-Client-Version` and we lose the signal downstream.
aj: if header normalization is the culprit, telemetry should show an inbound header event and then a downstream routing decision event. do we have a trace?
maria: attaching trace link: https://trace.internal/r-0a9b3f (paste) — you can see `header_v2=true` at ingress and `route=v1` in router.
opsbot: deploy/infra — auth-proxy v1.12.3 deployed to prod at 2024-11-01T09:12:30Z :rocket:
pm_sarah: product question — if some customers see console 'v2 enabled' but actually routed to v1, that's a bad UX. we need a clear dashboard indicator and a customer-facing explanation for the grace-fallback. can we show 'effective route' vs 'requested version'?
devon: agreed. immediate fix is to add a small telemetry mapping that emits both requested_version and effective_route in the same span. then console can surface the mismatch. also add a short-lived metric: `version_mismatch_count`.
samir: long term we should avoid silent fallbacks. propose a rollout: shadow cohort (1% traffic) where we emit mismatch alerts to the tenant owners, then escalate to 10% if no regressions. also consider a hard-fail flag for opt-in customers.
aj: practical mitigation: quick patch in router — prefer header from auth-proxy trace context if present. fallback order: explicit header -> token metadata -> server default. adding that ordering patch should reduce these cases.
maria: what about quotas? I noticed those tenants got billed at v1 rates in billing panel, which is wrong for reports.
devon: billing uses the effective model id. if we change routing order mid-billing period we may double count. safe approach: annotate billing events with `requested_version` and `effective_version` so we can reconcile retroactively.
pm_sarah: timeline? ops needs a small rollout plan + console mock. can design do a banner: "Requested version differs from effective route — contact support" with a drilldown.
aj: patch PR is small. I'll open it now: https://git.internal/pr/3421 — includes router ordering + unit tests. CI green locally.
aj: deploy plan: canary in t1 region (5%), monitor `version_mismatch_count`, `p50_latency`, and `billing_event_tags`. rollback if mismatch > 0.5% of requests or billing anomalies detected.
samir: add an alerting rule to paging that triggers if mismatch spikes for any single tenant above 0.2% over 15m. we want owner visibility before customer tickets.
maria: ok — I'll add the console panel change to the dashboard ticket (T-4982) and include example copy. can someone review the copy?
pm_sarah: i'll review and add a UX for the drilldown. include wording: "Effective route may differ due to compatibility fallbacks; see per-request details."
devon: one last nit — make sure we include case-insensitive header parsing in the proxy + preserve original header case in telemetry so we can debug later.
aj: ack. landing PR, will start canary tomorrow at 16:00 UTC. will post progress here. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks everyone. tagging @support on the console banner draft once it's in T-4982.
opsbot: alert — canary started for router-ordering patch in region t1 at 2024-11-02T16:00:12Z. monitoring: version_mismatch_count, billing_event_tags.
